listingTitle: Avoid Java String concatenation in loops
title: Avoid Java String concatenation in loops
why: Repeated immutable String concatenation can copy the growing prefix on every iteration.
suggestion: Use StringBuilder when only the final String is needed. If the loop consumes each intermediate String, preserve that behavior and profile before changing it.
limitations: Only explicitly declared String variables whose nearest declaration precedes a braced loop are checked.
Recognizes +=, accumulator-leading addition, and simple identifier + accumulator prepending assignments. Literal or compound prepend expressions and flow-sensitive resets are not inferred.
Intermediate prefix consumers can require String materialization inside the loop; a finding is not proof that converting only after the loop preserves behavior or improves performance.
